result.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
result.summary: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid from invalid overor under-segmentation. We present Star Panoptic Quality (StarPQ), a novel evaluation ramework, which closes this gap in two steps: First, we construct a so-called star forest in the bipartite graph whose clean, merge, and split stars isolate different failure modes. Second, we calculate the final metric by individually weighting each failure mode, allowing practitioners to account for instance delineation biases. Across various experiments, we demonstrate that StarPQ not only enables targeted penalization or eniency towards specific failure modes, but also serves as a diagnostic tool to reveal their prevalence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 StarPQ 评价框架：在预测与参考实例的二分图中构造 star forest，将 clean、merge、split 三类失败模式分离，再按模式分别加权，使参考标注有偏时也能有针对性地评估全景分割质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将实例匹配失败分解为合并／分裂并分项加权的诊断思路，可能可供核查于刻画 latent 视觉状态中实体被合并、拆分或信息坍缩的情形；但原文仅为分割评测指标，未涉及推理期状态生成。
